metadata.statement_scope: Exactly Theorem4.2 in the genus g>=2 Mumford-curve branch. In particular any linear algebraic group generated Zariski-densely by at most g elements is realizable on X. No claim that every rigid stratification is locally trivial or that every algebraic group is realizable over this fixed X is made.

metadata.title: Universal prismatic G-mu-display deformations for smooth affine groups over Zp and one-bounded cocharacters, on complete regular local Witt-vector bases
metadata.author: Kazuhiro Ito
metadata.source_version: Forum of Mathematics, Sigma volume 13 (2025), article e61, official publisher downloaded version of record with publisher acquisition stamp retained

source_locator.theorem: Theorem1.1.3, existence part of Theorem4.1.7 in the Zp setting
source_locator.selected_scope: Fix a prime p, a perfect field k of characteristic p, a smooth affine group scheme G over Zp and a cocharacter mu:G_m->G_(W(k)) that is one-bounded in the exact inverse-conjugation Lie-weight convention of Definition2.3.1 (all such weights are at most1). For any G-mu-display Q over the bounded prism(W(k),(p)), there exists a universal deformation as a prismatic G-mu-display over R_(G,mu), the completed local ring at the identity of U_mu_minus defined by lim_(t->0) mu(t)^(-1)g mu(t)=1. Universality means that for each complete regular local W(k)-algebra R_prime with residue field k and each deformation of Q over R_prime, a unique local W(k)-homomorphism R_(G,mu)->R_prime pulls back this universal deformation to it, up to an isomorphism respecting the given reduction to Q. The deformation is not required to be banal or adjoint-nilpotent. Only the primary existence/universality statement on this exact regular-local category is counted: no arbitrary artinian or quasisyntomic-base assertion, separate truncated/perfectoid evaluation property, tangent criterion, F-gauge equivalence, local Shimura or p-divisible-group classification is counted.

metadata.title: Aperiodic countable Borel equivalence relations admit proper Borel wallings exactly when they are Borel treeable
metadata.author: Ruiyuan Chen, Antoine Poulin, Ran Tao and Anush Tserunyan
metadata.source_version: Forum of Mathematics, Sigma volume 13 (2025), article e64, official publisher downloaded version of record with publisher acquisition stamp retained

source_locator.selected_scope: Let E be a countable Borel equivalence relation on a standard Borel space X, with every equivalence class countably infinite. Then E admits a proper Borel walling in the precise sense of Definitions2.53 and4.1/4.2 if and only if E admits a Borel forest graphing with connectedness relation E. A walling assigns to each class C a subpocset of its powerset, containing the empty/full subsets and closed under complement, with the finite-separation condition. Properness requires finite indistinguishability blocks, only finitely many nonnested walls for each wall, and only finitely many nontrivial successor walls. The assignment must be Borel in the exact class-powerset bundle of Definition4.2; no mere per-class nonuniform existence is sufficient. This is one primary abstract characterization, not separate quasi-tree, bounded-treewidth, subtreeing, quasi-isometry or one-end hyperfiniteness counts.

metadata.title: Cofinite Ramsey classification of countably infinite connected trees in two edge colours
metadata.author: Jan Corsten; Louis DeBiasio; Paul McKenney

source_locator.theorem: Theorem1.14, both primary directions, restricted to countably infinite connected trees
source_locator.selected_scope: Let T be a countably infinite connected tree. It is Ramsey-cofinite for two edge colours if it is strongly contracting, has no finite dominating set and does not belong to the exceptional family T-star; if it is weakly expanding, has a finite dominating set or belongs to T-star, it is not even Ramsey-lower-dense. Ramsey-cofinite means every red-blue colouring of the complete graph on the natural numbers has a monochromatic subgraph isomorphic to T whose vertex set is cofinite; Ramsey-lower-dense asks for positive lower asymptotic density. Strong contraction means there is a fixed nonnegative k such that arbitrarily large finite independent sets have at most k neighbours; weak expansion is its source-defined complementary quantified property. A finite dominating set has a neighbour of every vertex outside it. T-star consists of trees with one vertex t of infinite degree, all other vertices of degree at most some common finite d, t adjacent to infinitely many leaves and infinitely many non-leaves, and all but finitely many vertices at distance at most two from t. source_locator.proof_scope: Theorem3.6: arbitrary color set C, total preorder preference on C^omega, fixed finite deterministic memory skeleton M with fixed initial state and color-update function. source_locator.proof_scope: First-order signatures and formulas in the source constructive Coq type-theoretic setting. FSAT means a model on a list-finite inhabited domain with decidable relation interpretations; domain equality is initially unrestricted. Every such satisfiable formula has a model on a finite discrete domain, and conversely, giving the two identity many-one reductions FSAT and FSAT0. The authors build a bounded-signature indistinguishability congruence as a greatest fixed point, prove computable stabilization through an enumerated weak powerset, and transport the model through an explicit decidable quotient. The result removes domain discreteness while retaining finite first-order satisfaction, an independent constructive model-theory obligation beyond the usual classical finite-model argument.

metadata.title: Constructively, pointwise convergence on a complete metric space gives the Third Trick dichotomy along a convergent sequence, and its counterexample alternative implies LPO
metadata.author: Hannes Diener; Matthew Hendtlass
metadata.source_title: The Third Trick
metadata.source_version: LMCS volume18 issue3 article21 (nominal2022), DOI 10.46298/LMCS-18(3:21)2022; current unchanged official download acquired 2026-10-01T18:22:07.144806+00:00; actual PDF publication/header identity retained in source_header_identity

source_locator.proof_scope: In Bishop constructive mathematics with the source dependent/countable choice assumptions, let f_n:X->Y converge pointwise to f, where X is a complete metric space and Y any metric space. Given x_n->x and epsilon>0, either there is N such that for all n,i>=N the distance between f(x_n) and f_i(x_n) is less than epsilon, or there are z_n->x and k_n>=n with distance between f_{k_n}(z_n) and f(z_n) greater than epsilon/4 for every n. In the second alternative, LPO holds. No continuity or strong extensionality of the functions is assumed.

metadata.difficulty_reason: The proof cannot decide an arbitrary real inequality or invoke excluded middle for the existence of a nonuniform witness. It replaces exact tests by three separated error thresholds, constructs Cauchy sequences that freeze at the first flagged violation, and then extracts the uniform alternative or an infinite witness from pointwise convergence at their limits. A further freezing construction turns the witness into the limited principle of omniscience, making the constructive obligation substantially stronger than the classical dichotomy.
